I reproduced 372,378 bills / 354 days only with window >='2025-09-01' (not the declared 2025-08-31, which gives 373,461 bills / 355 days), NO warehouse restriction, and NO 002CM exclusion. Snack sales Rs 41,47,393 reproduces only on the same unfiltered base (declared base wh 9/11/15 excl 002CM gives Rs 40,54,018). refuted.claim: '31 of the 42 best days sit in the four richest snack months'
refuted.why: Not reproducible under any reading. The monthly table itself verifies cell-for-cell, so I tested every definition of 'richest' against it. By snack Rs/bill the four richest are 2025-09 (14.12), 2026-02 (13.05), 2025-10 (12.88), 2025-12 (12.13), holding 6+6+8+5 = 25 of the 42 n=8 days. By total snack rupees the four richest are 2025-09, 2026-05, 2025-10, 2026-04 = 19 days. Reaching 31 requires the set {Mar-26, Oct-25, Sep-25, Dec-25}, and Mar-26 is the SEVENTH richest month by Rs/bill (11.03). The confounding argument still stands directionally at 25 of 42 (60%), but the published number overstates it.
refuted.correctedNumber: 25 of the 42 best days (not 31). The companion clause verifies exactly: 23 of the 45 worst days are in Dec-25 (11) and Jul-26 (12).

refuted.claim: Whole-bill average is higher on bare-shelf days (Rs 246.69) than full-shelf days (Rs 238.65)
refuted.why: Both numbers verify to the paisa, but the inference drawn from them is unsupported by the row the note omits. The 267-day middle band (n=5-7, ~273k bills — 73% of the year) averages Rs 192.68 per bill, 22% BELOW both cited extremes. The relationship is not monotone and not even ordered; the two quoted bands are the two smallest and the note reports only them. Presenting this as 'the opposite of what the brief implies' treats a non-relationship as a directional finding. The conservative conclusion it supports (don't extrapolate to the till) is right, but this evidence does not support it.
refuted.correctedNumber: Rs 246.69 (n<=4, 45 days) / Rs 192.68 (n=5-7, 267 days) / Rs 238.65 (n=8, 42 days) — no monotone relationship
